question_text: State the modern periodic law.
easy_answer: Properties repeat periodically with atomic number.

question_text: How many periods are there in the modern periodic table?
easy_answer: There are 7 periods.

question_text: How many groups are there in the modern periodic table?
easy_answer: There are 18 groups.

question_text: What is a group in the periodic table?
easy_answer: A group is a vertical column.

question_text: What is a period?
easy_answer: A period is a horizontal row.

question_text: What are valence electrons?
easy_answer: Outer-shell electrons are valence electrons.

question_text: Why do elements of the same group show similar chemical properties?
easy_answer: Similar valence electrons give similar properties.

question_text: What is periodicity?
easy_answer: Periodic repetition of properties is periodicity.

question_text: Where are metals generally found in the periodic table?
hint: Non-metals are mainly on the right.
easy_answer: Metals occupy left and centre regions.

question_text: Where are non-metals generally found?
easy_answer: Most non-metals are on the right.

question_text: What is the general valency of noble gases?
easy_answer: Noble gases generally have valency zero.

question_text: Why is sodium highly reactive?
easy_answer: Sodium readily loses its one valence electron.

question_text: What happens to atomic size across a period from left to right?
hint: Nuclear charge increases while shells remain same.
easy_answer: Atomic size generally decreases.

question_text: What happens to atomic size down a group?
hint: A new electron shell is added.
easy_answer: Atomic size increases down a group.

question_text: What is ionization energy?
hint: It is energy for electron removal.
easy_answer: Ionization energy is energy required to remove an electron.

question_text: What is electronegativity?
easy_answer: It is attraction for shared electrons.

question_text: What is a period number related to?
hint: For main-group elements, period indicates shells.
easy_answer: Period number corresponds to occupied shells.

question_text: Why is fluorine highly electronegative?
easy_answer: Fluorine has very high attraction for electrons.

question_text: Name the element with atomic number 11.
easy_answer: Z = 11 is sodium.
